messages.text: Next step is to get familiar with the Open Data Detector - try to find all necessary resources and either register where they are (and download them for reading if print-style-only)

I’ll inventory the Open Data Detector’s source repository, documentation and publications, then register the useful resources in our catalogue. I’ll download relevant PDF-only material for later reading and keep the baseline revision choice explicit.

I found the canonical CERN GitLab repository, its archived releases, and the ACTS integration documentation. I’m also checking the ODD presentations and newer ColliderML material, because they describe different stages of the detector and should not be treated as one configuration.

The upstream checkout already contains tracker, calorimeter and muon factories, plus staged XML entry points and CI checks for construction, overlaps, material and simulation. That is newer than the presentations describing muons as future work. I’m recording the exact study revision and these differences so later baseline selection is informed by the code.

The core resource set is assembled. The PDF presentations are downloaded and searchable; the web-readable manuals and papers will be registered by URL. One useful caution is already clear: the ACTS tutorial’s magnetic-field setup differs from the inspected ODD XML, so we’ll need to select geometry, field and reconstruction settings together for a reproducible baseline.

The resource guide is written with source links, a map of the upstream code, PDF reading locations and version caveats. Four PDFs are cached—107 pages in total—and their retrieval and integrity checks pass. The remaining decisions concern which ODD revision and toolchain to characterize; the study checkout does not select that baseline.

Created the [ODD resource guide]([redacted] covering **21 resources**:

- Canonical source repository, releases and source-code navigation.
- ACTS integration, material mapping and reconstruction.
- DD4hep, Geant4 and Key4hep documentation.
- ODD presentations, TrackML history and ColliderML resources.

**Downloaded and indexed four PDFs—107 pages—and obtained an ignored study checkout** with its exact revision and file hashes recorded.

The inspected code already includes tracker, calorimeter and muon factories. The guide flags differences between historical presentations, current source and tutorial configurations.

Checks passed: PDF/source integrity, four retrieval checks, 15 documentation/logging tests and 12 session records. ACAT 2021 attachments remain an optional access gap.

Changes are **uncommitted on `main`**. No detector build or baseline selection occurred.

Next: trace one ODD pixel module from XML through its factory and service helpers to understand the existing modelling conventions.
